D-023's scope repair is the strongest work in the draft — it is explicitly non-exhaustive and now reaches analyze's data plane. Consensus is nevertheless not available, on two structural defects the split itself introduced. First, D-020 and D-022 carry no operative text: their Decision sections incorporate D-019's clauses by reference, so reverting C-D019 would strand them, defeating the per-entry revert independence the draft asserts. Second, the shared recording rule — a block explicitly labelled 'not itself a decision' and referenced by five entries — asserts that the coordinator may author disposition bytes 'on the owner's behalf under D-000', but D-000 delegates only coordinator/product-authority decisions, and file 08 names the V1 coordinator as co-owner for only two of the five rows (DR-002, DR-003); DR-004, DR-005 and DR-008's contract half have no coordinator owner at all. D-017's own Route C repair gets this distinction right, which shows the draft can state it correctly. Under D-000 turn 3 of 3 these park CONTESTED rather than being forced to consensus.

objections.claim: D-020 and D-022 have no operative text of their own. Their Decision sections incorporate D-019's clauses by reference, so neither is independently revertible in substance — reverting C-D019 would strand both — which contradicts the per-entry revert independence the draft asserts as the answer to turn 2's bundling finding.
objections.evidence: D-020's entire Decision section (L139-141) reads: 'Same three operative clauses as D-019, with every "DR-002" replaced by "DR-004". Shared rationale. Shared recording rule. Writes no Phase-1A packet. Marks nothing SATISFIED.' D-022's (L184-185) reads: 'Same three operative clauses as D-019, restricted to the integration half. Shared rationale. Shared recording rule.' Neither states what it selects, for what scope, what it does not do, or what a completed disposition may discharge — all three of which live only inside D-019 Decision 1-3 (L108-116). The draft's own severability claims are then unsupportable: D-019's overturn (L126-127) says revert 'does not revert D-020..D-024', and D-020's overturn (L145) is 'C-D020 only.' But if each entry is copied into COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md as its own C-D0xx commit, reverting C-D019 removes the only copy of D-020's and D-022's operative clauses, leaving two adopted entries pointing at reverted text. The draft asserts the correct principle at L65 — 'A common rationale is not a common revert unit' — and then shares more than rationale: it shares the operative clauses themselves. This is the same defect class as turn-1's C2-D018-01 and turn-2's ADV-D019-T2-01, displaced one level down rather than resolved.
objections.proposedFix: Write D-020's and D-022's three operative clauses out in full, substituting the row and scope. Reserve cross-entry reference for the shared rationale, which is genuinely non-operative. Once each entry carries its own operative bytes, the per-entry overturn clauses become true as written.

objections.claim: The shared recording rule asserts a D-000 delegation scope that D-000's text does not grant. D-000 delegates coordinator and product-authority decisions; three of the five owning authorities named by these entries are neither. The assertion sits in a block explicitly labelled 'not itself a decision' and is operatively referenced by all five Route B entries.
objections.evidence: Shared recording rule L73-76: 'If the coordinator authors disposition bytes on the owner's behalf under D-000, independent review is still required and does not replace the owner cell in file 08.' D-000's grant, measured at COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md L26-27, is: 'The assistant completes the coop design end-to-end, making COORDINATOR/PRODUCT-AUTHORITY decisions on the user's behalf, under these terms.' Evidence authority, evidence/retention authority, storage authority, operability authority and threat-model authority are V1 surface authorities — neither coordinator nor product authority. Measured against file 08's owner cells: DR-002 is 'Evidence authority + V1 coordinator' and DR-003 is 'Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator', so the coordinator is a named CO-owner for two rows; but DR-004 is 'Evidence/retention authority', DR-005 is 'Evidence, storage, operability authorities', and DR-008's contract half is 'evidence/retention authority' — no coordinator owner at all for three of the five. Condition 1's alternative is conditioned on 'the owning V1 authority records' the disposition; if the coordinator both authors and records for those three rows under a delegation D-000 does not extend to them, condition 1 is not discharged and the Route B selections buy nothing. That extending D-000's delegation to V1 surface authorities would itself be a preference-laden decision requiring its own reviewed entry makes its placement in a block declared 'not itself a decision' worse than turn-1's bundling defect: a decision inside a non-decision block has no commit and therefore no revert at all. The draft demonstrates it can state the scope correctly — D-017's repaired Route C confines its D-000 branch to 'where the coordinator decides on the user's behalf', which is precisely the product-authority case D-000 does grant.
objections.proposedFix: Either (a) strike the delegation clause and state that the named owning authority records the disposition, with the coordinator drafting only; or (b) isolate the delegation extension as its own preference-laden entry under D-000 review, naming which surface authorities it covers and why, and have D-019..D-023 reference that entry rather than an assertion embedded in a non-decision block. Option (a) requires no new decision and is available now.

objections.claim: The two shared blocks are operatively referenced by five entries but have no adoption vehicle, no commit, and no revert path, so their status after any partial adoption or revert is undefined.
objections.evidence: The shared rationale (L54-65) and shared recording rule (L69-77) are each headed 'referenced by ...; not itself a decision.' Every Route B entry then relies on them operatively — D-019 Decision 1 'Shared rationale above. Shared recording rule above.', repeated in D-020, D-021, D-022, and D-023. The draft's adoption model, carried from turn 1 (L4-6 of the turn-1 draft and unchanged in practice), is that each entry is copied into COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and committed as its own C-D0xx. Nothing states where the shared blocks are copied, in which commit they land, or what happens to them if every referencing entry is reverted. If they are copied once, they survive the revert of all five referencing entries; if copied into each, they are duplicated and can diverge. Either outcome contradicts the draft's central severability claim at L65.
objections.proposedFix: Name the vehicle explicitly: either inline both blocks into each entry that relies on them, or adopt them as their own numbered entry with its own commit that D-019..D-023 cite by ID, and state what happens to that entry when all referencing entries are reverted.

objections.claim: The dual-track disclosure repair was applied to the instance turn 2 named (DR-005) but not to the class. DR-002, DR-004 and DR-008's integration half have the same preview-Route-B / authoritative-Route-A structure against Lane R, and none carries the equivalent statement.
objections.evidence: D-021 Decision 2 discloses that DR-005 is preview-scoped Route B while the authoritative V10/custody and G19 demonstration remains owed. D-024's Lane R (L254-257) names the authoritative counterparts of the other three by name: 'Identity recipes (DR-006), D9 (DR-007), Phase-1A as V1 successor work for the authoritative path, evidence/retention join, and V10/custody/G19.' 'Phase-1A' is DR-004, selected for preview Route B by D-020; the 'evidence/retention join' is DR-008's integration half, selected by D-022; and DR-002 (EVIDENCE) underlies both. So three further rows are dual-tracked across severable entries, exactly as DR-005 was, and only DR-005 says so. D-020's sole gesture at this is the fragment 'Writes no Phase-1A packet', which states what the entry does not do rather than what remains owed on the authoritative path. A reader adopting D-020 or D-022 without D-024 gets no statement that the authoritative work survives.
objections.proposedFix: Add to D-019, D-020 and D-022 the sentence pattern already proven in D-021 Decision 2, naming each row's authoritative counterpart and stating that it remains owed whether or not D-024 is adopted.

objections.claim: D-017 and D-024 use 'consume' for two different acts without distinguishing them, and D-024's consumption vehicle is not one of the three routes D-017's rule admits.
objections.evidence: D-017 Decision 3, retained from the turn-2 draft at 744ad8e3 and unamended except for Route C, states that an item in file 11 'becomes live work only by travelling a route D-001 §3 already names' — Route A, Route B, or Route C — and that 'Conversation, this draft, and file 11 itself satisfy none of A, B, or C.' D-024's File 11 accounting (L300-310) then states that 'Inclusion in this adopted sequence consumes the item as authorization to draft' and lists five items consumed that way. D-024 is a coordinator execution-sequence entry: it is not a V1 successor (Route A), not a pre-blueprint disposition (Route B), and not a product decision through the product-disposition process (Route C). The two are reconcilable if 'consume as authorization to draft' is a weaker act than 'becomes live work', with the drafted artifact still owing its own A/B/C passage — and D-024's rider 'Substantive outcomes remain open at the owning later artifacts' points that way. But neither entry says so, and D-017 is RULE-GOVERNED and is the entry that governs how file 11 is consumed. A corpus that treats one word carrying two meanings as a defect should not ship this one.
objections.proposedFix: Add one sentence to D-017 Decision 3 distinguishing the two: scheduling an item for drafting in an adopted coordinator sequence is not itself a route, and the resulting artifact still becomes live work only by travelling A, B or C. Then have D-024's accounting rule cite that sentence.

objections.evidence: The turn-1 and turn-2 drafts each carried, immediately below the inputs table: 'If a cited file moves before adoption, the citing sentence is re-measured. A moved source is not silently treated as the same source.' Measured: the string 'moved source is not silently treated' occurs once in the turn-2 draft and zero times in the turn-3 draft. Meanwhile the turn-3 inputs table (L32) pins COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 3f449778932876ab5039c7f4b35a136a06a67c06b4e2ec00a70e95ae5f3c313f, and I measure it at review time as af4b24c3d2266c731f58e9add4e17e733d3510e7d09d48efc5b2c69678821e6a — moved by the D-018 adoption at commit 6969f72, which is HEAD. I do NOT raise the stale digest itself as a finding against the draft: the move occurred after authoring, and a post-authoring move must never present as a defect in the subject. What I raise is the removal of the handling rule. This is a whole-document pin supporting claims about specific sections (D-002's deferral reason, D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03), which is the defect form freeze §7.10 warns against and which re-opens DR-001 on every freeze edit; the draft's own sibling decision stranded it within the same day.
objections.proposedFix: Restore the re-measurement clause verbatim from the turn-2 draft, and re-measure COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md to af4b24c3d2266c731f58e9add4e17e733d3510e7d09d48efc5b2c69678821e6a before adoption. Better, cite the two sections used (D-002's State paragraph and D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03) by anchor and segment hash rather than pinning the whole document.

objections.claim: The non-exhaustive surface list sits inside a closed five-category frame that does not obviously admit two surfaces D-002 actually ships.
objections.evidence: D-023 Decision 2 opens: 'The later disposition's scope is every D-002 command, input, process/protocol, state, and output boundary.' The twelve-item list beneath it is correctly marked non-exhaustive, but the frame that governs it is a closed five-category enumeration. Two D-002 surfaces do not sit cleanly in any of the five: the supported-platform matrix (D-002 selects macOS arm64/x86_64 and Linux x86_64/arm64, and platform-specific filesystem permission and credential-store behaviour is threat-model-relevant), and the install/trust surface (D-002 defers DR-110 with 'install is fresh signed download in slice 1', which makes first-install trust in scope even though self-update is not). 'Signed delivery' in the list gestures at the second but the frame does not name a trust or platform boundary category. Since the list's non-exhaustiveness is what makes the repair work, a frame narrower than the list would undercut it.
objections.proposedFix: Either widen the frame — 'every D-002 command, input, process/protocol, state, output, platform, and trust boundary' — or replace it with an open formulation such as 'every boundary D-002 actually ships, including but not limited to the following.'

terminationNote: This is turn 3 of 3. Two MUST-FIX findings survive against D-019..D-023 and are not discharged in the start bytes, so CONSENT is unavailable on any entry in the subject and I do not offer one. Under D-000 clause 2 these park CONTESTED with both positions recorded and batch to the user; work proceeds on other surfaces. I record explicitly that both surviving MUST-FIXes are narrow and mechanically repairable — C2T3-D020-01 requires writing two entries' operative clauses out in full, and C2T3-SHARED-01 requires striking one clause or isolating it as its own entry — so a turn-4 cycle, if the coordinator judges one lawful under a fresh dispatch rather than as a fourth turn of this one, would likely converge.
